subtitle.overview: Manage connected iWorkerCenter instances for compute distribution, skill market, licensing, upgrades, and integration. iWorkerCloud is not an enterprise operations platform.
subtitle.centers: Register, authorize, and manage connected multi-tenant iWorkerCenter deployments.
subtitle.compute: Distribute model capacity, provider routes, quota policy, and usage billing.
subtitle.skills: Package, publish, authorize, and roll out top-level iWorker skills.

cloudOverview.title: Vendor cloud control plane for iWorker
cloudOverview.desc: iWorkerCloud is the management center for connected iWorkerCenter instances. It manages compute distribution, skill-market supply, commercial authorization, upgrades, and integration; it does not run customer companies.
cloudOverview.positionDesc: Customer company management and enterprise execution stay inside their own iWorkerCenter. iWorkerCloud only manages the system services we provide: compute, skills, authorization, upgrades, and integration.
cloudOverview.statCenters: Connected iWorkerCenter instances managed for system services.
cloudOverview.statPending: iWorkerCenter deployments waiting for activation, commercial review, or trial approval.
cloudOverview.statLicenses: Active paid or trial entitlements issued by our cloud platform.
cloudOverview.computeSummary: Borrowing the Hub-style provider coordination idea, Cloud owns the commercial compute pool and distributes capacity through connected iWorkerCenters.
cloudOverview.computeDetail: Providers, model routes, quota, pricing, and usage metering are controlled here. A multi-tenant iWorkerCenter consumes cloud-managed capacity or receives permission to self-manage routes.
cloudOverview.marketSummary: Our best reusable iWorker skills should be packaged once, sold or authorized through Cloud, then distributed to connected multi-tenant iWorkerCenters.
cloudOverview.marketDetail: Cloud governs skill listing, version rollout, entitlement, and retirement. The iWorkerCenter receives the skill and maps it into its own tenants, roles, workflows, and policy layer.
cloudOverview.tenantSummary: Cloud integrates with multi-tenant iWorkerCenter instances, then manages authorization, commercial access, modules, upgrades, compute and skill services at the Center boundary.
cloudOverview.tenantDetail: This is the management-center view for our company: Cloud does not recreate tenant organizations and does not participate in enterprise operations. It manages connected iWorkerCenter instances and their system-service capabilities.

skills.title: Top-level iWorker Skill Market
skills.desc: Package elite skills once, authorize them by center or tenant policy, and roll them out through connected multi-tenant iWorkerCenters without confusing Cloud with customer execution.
skills.positionDesc: Cloud sells and distributes skills. The connected iWorkerCenter decides how the skill enters each tenant organization, role, workflow, policy, and audit trail.

executive.title: Executive operating report skill
executive.summary: Packages optional executive reporting capability for iWorkerCenter customers.
executive.detail: Cloud can distribute this as a premium skill. The connected iWorkerCenter decides how the customer uses it inside its own governance boundaries.

recovery.title: Recovery institutionalization skill
recovery.summary: Converts recovered exceptions into memory, package, workflow, and policy-monitoring assets.
recovery.detail: This skill helps customers compound organizational capability instead of leaving recovery knowledge in one worker body or human memory.

compute.title: Compute optimization skill
compute.summary: Analyzes Center-level system usage and recommends model routing, quota, and cost policy for platform management.
compute.detail: This should sit close to Cloud's compute distribution layer and help our operators tune cost, latency, and product packaging.
